papers.title: Evaluation of the possibility of obtaining spherical powders of titanium alloy Ti 6Al 4V by supersonic reverse polarity plasma torch for use in additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: This work demonstrates the possibility of producing spherical Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5 alloy powders with superior technological properties compared to those obtained through conventional industrial gas atomization methods for additive manufacturing, by utilizing plasma atomization of a 1.0 mm diameter solid wire.The process employs supersonic plasma jets generated by a DC reverse polarity plasma torch with vortex arc stabilization.The plasma torch has a copper hollow electrode-anode and a special diffusive nozzle-cathode.Analysis of the particle size distribution of the powder showed the main fraction of -140 m 96 wt%, and the amount of the finely-divided fraction of -63 m is up to 55-60 wt%.Also, using subsonic jet had been give fraction -250 m, which is 97 wt%, and the amount of the finely-divided fraction -63 m does not exceed 30 wt%.The study of the shape and structure properties of Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5 powder showed that the sphericity coefficient reaches up to 0.9, the number of defects in the form of satellites and irregular particles does not exceed 1 wt%.In terms of technological characteristics, Ti-6Al-4V Grade 5 powder obtained by the adopted technique is on par with the industrial method of producing spherical powders for additive manufactuing by the direct polarity plasma torches.
papers.venue: Advances in Science and Technology – Research Journal

summary_zh.motivation: 探索通过等离子雾化制备球形Ti-6Al-4V粉末用于增材制造。
summary_zh.method: 采用直流反向极性等离子炬超音速射流雾化1.0 mm实心线材。
summary_zh.result: 获得球形度高、缺陷少的粉末，主要粒径分布为-140 μm占96 wt%。
summary_zh.validation: 通过粒径分析和球形度检测验证粉末质量。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the feasibility of producing spherical Ti-6Al-4V powders via plasma atomization for additive manufacturing feedstock.
summary_en.method: A supersonic reverse polarity DC plasma torch atomizes a 1.0 mm solid wire.
summary_en.result: Spherical powders with high sphericity and low defect content were obtained, with a main fraction of -140 μm at 96 wt%.
summary_en.validation: Particle size analysis and sphericity measurement confirmed the powder quality.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Driven Optimization of Computer Numerical Control Milling Parameters for Enhanced Surface Integrity and Burr Control in Additive Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive experimental and machine learning-based investigation into the effects of critical machining parameters—cutting speed (S), feed rate (F), and cutting depth (dp) on the burr formation and surface roughness (Ra) during computer numerical control milling of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V alloy. Statistical analyses, including factorial and one-way analysis of variance, identified cutting depth as the most influential parameter affecting burr formation (F = 171.379, p &lt; 0.001), while cutting speed had the greatest effect on surface roughness (F = 39.324, p &lt; 0.001). Burr formation ranged from 0.09 mm to 1.46 mm, and surface roughness varied between 0.07 µm and 0.22 µm, highlighting the sensitivity of machining performance to process parameters. To model and predict machining outcomes, six machine learning algorithms—decision tree, random forest, K-nearest neighbors, gradient boosting, LightGBM, and CatBoost were evaluated. Gradient boosting achieved the highest predictive accuracy for burr formation (test R2 &gt; 0.98), while LightGBM and gradient boosting also performed best for Ra prediction (test R2 &gt; 0.81). Feature importance and Shapley additive explanations analysis using XGBoost revealed that cutting depth contributed over 90% to burr formation prediction, reaffirming its dominant role. The integration of statistical and machine learning approaches enabled a dual-response optimization strategy, minimizing burrs while enhancing surface quality, providing a data-driven framework for precision process control. These findings offer actionable insights for high-performance machining of Ti-6Al-4V and underscore the value of intelligent optimization techniques in advanced manufacturing applications.

papers.title: Piezodynamic Behavior of HA-BT Osteoconductive Coatings Under LIPUS Stimulation in Lab-on-a-Chip Model: A Promising Strategy for Bone Regeneration
papers.abstract: Bone regeneration demands biomaterials capable of supporting tissue integration and mimicking the native piezodynamic properties of bone. In this study, hydroxyapatite–barium titanate (HA-BT) composite coatings with varying BT content (10, 30, and 50 wt%) were developed to enhance the piezoelectric response and corrosion resistance of Ti6Al4V implants. The coatings were synthesized via high-energy ball milling and atmospheric plasma spraying (APS). XRD analysis with Rietveld refinement confirmed the presence of HA along with secondary phases (TTCP, β-TCP, CaO). Electrochemical tests revealed lower corrosion current densities for the coatings containing ≤30% BT, indicating improved stability in physiological environments. Cytotoxicity assays (MTT) demonstrated biocompatibility across all formulations. Piezoresponse force microscopy (DART-SS-PFM) confirmed enhanced d33-eff values for the 50% BT coating (>15 pm/V); however, biological assays under low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) stimulation showed increased osteocalcin expression for ≤30% BT, while 50% BT induced cellular stress. Overall, HA-BT coatings with up to 30% BT exhibited optimal electrochemical stability, favorable piezoelectric performance, and enhanced biological response, underscoring their potential for orthopedic implant applications and regenerative tissue engineering.
